name: Old Billingsgate Market
text: Old Billingsgate is the name given to what is now a hospitality and events venue in the City of London, based in the Victorian building that was originally Billingsgate Fish Market, the world's largest fish market in the 19th century. The first Billingsgate Market building was constructed on Lower Thames Street in 1850 by the builder John Jay, and the fish market was moved off the streets into its new riverside building. This was demolished in around 1873 and replaced by an arcaded market hall designed by City of London architect Horace Jones and built by John Mowlem & Co. in 1875, the building that still stands on the site today.
